newsitem.title: USA: US high-yield corporate bonds weaker on stock drop.
newsitem.headline: US high-yield corporate bonds weaker on stock drop.

text.p: The U.S. high-yield corporate bond market weakened on Monday as market players watched the stock market sell-off with growing concern, traders said.
"People are sitting back watching the stock market," said one junk trader. "Junk bond prices are down about one point across the board, but we're not seeing much trading right now," he added.
Another junk trader said, "The market is still feeling the effects from the Greenspan speech a month ago. This market is having the 'exuberance' taken out of it."

Market players said a severe correction in the stock market could be the latest malady to afflict junk bonds, which have seen spreads widen by around 80 basis points on average from historically tight levels several weeks ago.

Values in the junk bond and equity markets are related, in part, because many junk bond issuers are counting on being able to raise money in the stock market over the next several years in order to pay back their bondholders.
Other factors contributing to recent junk-bond weakness was a recent sell-off in Treasuries as well as comments by the Federal Reserve Chairman that junk bonds were overvalued.
Last week, investors pulled $422 million of funds out of high-yield mutual funds, further adding to weak technicals in the market.
In the high-grade market, volume was similarly low on Monday, although price levels held firm to Treasuries.

Traders noted, however, that weakness in the junk bond market caused spreads in some lower-quality investment-grade bonds, particularly in the cable and media sector, to widened by around one basis point.
Early on Monday, several money managers distributed bid lists totalling around $100 million in high-grade debt.
Traders said the bid lists were quickly absorbed by the market and did not affect spreads.
The new issue market, which tends to be slow early in the week, was particularly quiet on Monday.
Syndicate sources said several large deals were in the works for later this week, such as multi-tranche bond offering by J.C. Penney Co of at least $2 billion.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 157.11 points in a day of heavy trading.
The price of the benchmark 30-year Treasury dropped 5/32 to 94-4/32. Its yield rose to 7.10 percent.
